reference_components.adopt: one application owner composes components but does not own their business semantics
components emit typed intents into one bus instead of calling application internals
keep transcript composition separate from individual cell rendering
committed history and mutable streaming cells have stable identity and distinct lifecycle
typed render inputs, layout ownership, measurement and cursor ownership
composer, approval, question, command and selectors are mutually owned interaction views
one owner controls focus, pending input and modal replacement
raw mode, alternate screen, paste, resize, suspend, signals and restoration are one resource
invalidate and coalesce frames; avoid an unconditional fixed-rate render loop

reasons: matches the DSH Node runtime family without Bun or native FFI
provides alternate-screen lifecycle, paste, resize, focus, cursor and measurement primitives
supports deterministic string rendering and established component tests
keeps business projection and Cordis plugin ownership outside React
constraints: Ink is a rendering carrier, not the component registry or business state owner
renderer plugins receive canonical view nodes and emit typed UI intents only
terminal lifecycle is wrapped by one Cordis resource and verified in a real PTY
the dependency is exact-version pinned and must pass clean-registry installation

rejected.reason: its native renderer currently requires Node 26.4 with experimental FFI or Bun, adding a runtime and native-package boundary outside the installation target
older mutable widget model, weaker current TypeScript and lifecycle fit than Ink
duplicates layout, focus, wide-character and terminal restoration owners
violates the Node/Cordis-only architecture and reintroduces an unnecessary bridge protocol
